data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2021 gross claims outstanding were $175.11m. Analysis of the gross claims development table indicates a net prioryear release of approximately $8.01m (c. -4.6% of opening reserves), driven by favourable development in the older underwriting years (notably 2017 and 2018) partly offset by adverse movement in 2019. Management narrative also notes an overall deterioration on prior year reserves of GBP 2.626m (reported net), and highlights uncertainty due to reliance on cedant/bordereau data and reinsurance recoveries. Stresstest scenarios (terrorism, AEP catastrophe events, cyber, marine and aviation scenarios) are disclosed and considered in reserving and capital assessments.
raw_causal_phrases: This reliance and lack of source data adds an extra layer of uncertainty in relation to estimating claims provisions.

In particular, judgement is applied when estimating the value of amounts that should be provided for claims that have been incurred at the reporting date but have not yet been reported (IBNR) to the Syndicate.
In 2021, there has been an overall deterioration of GBP 2,626k on prior year reserves (2020: deficit GBP 11,576k).

The Directors consider that the gross provision for claims and the related reinsurance recoveries are fairly stated based on the information currently available to them, however the ultimate liability will vary as a result of subsequent information and events.
data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development computed from the gross claims development table (triangle) on pages 43-44 resulting in a $8.01m release. This conflicts with a narrative sentence reporting an overall deterioration of GBP 2,626k (likely a net of reinsurance figure reported in GBP). RITC activity (2019 & prior reinsured to Syndicate 1254 as at 31/12/2021) and reliance on cedant/AXA XL bordereaux may distort development patterns. Gross triangle was used as primary gross source; narrative net GBP figure used for verbatim quote only.
